cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you set down is being weighed as you write it.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Show one person how you see something before it's settled — the working version, not the findings. Let them try it beside you for a few minutes, and change it if their hands find a better way.
cells.core:
Where only the shape of a thing remains, you can see how it works and hold that steady enough to hand on. When the shape is clear you say it plainly, at a size the moment can carry, and that is what makes the clarity useful to anyone else.

What comes next is showing someone the pattern while it's working, not once it's finished. You don't have to have it settled to pass it over. Say the version you have now to one person who's in this with you, and stay while they try it. That kind of sharing carries what a finished explanation wouldn't, and you'll feel what you actually know by watching it move.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape and say it plainly.
cells.verb: holding clear sight steady until what is true can be said well
cells.place: out past the literal, where only the shape of the thing remains

cells.tense: You will have it all worked out before you say a word, and the moment to say it keeps sliding further out.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Pick the smallest piece of this you could say today — one sentence, not the whole case. Say it before you're sure of the rest, then stop. Tomorrow, add one more.
cells.core:
The pattern is being run to its end before any of it gets said. Every version you could offer gets a better version raised over it, and the versions stack until the saying keeps slipping to next week. It feels like getting it right. It is closer to waiting for airtight, and airtight is where things stop breathing.

What this wants is steady feeding, not force. One sentence today, said before it's whole. Tomorrow one more. The readiness you're waiting for comes from the saying, not before it. Keep a small fire under this instead of a bonfire, and give it something daily — a line said, a half-thought handed over. The rest of the clarity shows up once the first piece is out of your hands.

cells.tense: You stood at that door with everything clear, and you are still standing there.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask someone close how something has been for them, and stay with what comes back — five minutes, no fixing, no improving. Let your own answer wait until they're done.
cells.core:
The shape was clear and you saw it, and none of it has landed anywhere since. You can still describe how the thing works. What's missing is the part where it touches anyone, including you, and you know the difference even when you'd rather not say it.

What returns you is someone else's answer, held without adjusting it. Ask a person near you how it has been, and stay with whatever they give. Five minutes, no fixing, no improving. Hold your own ground while you do — you don't have to feel it with them to be there. That kind of company does something in you that analysis can't, and it's the shortest route to being present again.

cells.tense: You are writing in a room you already belong to, and the pen is down.
cells.act: make a ritual of the shared thing
cells.ask: Pick the thing you and someone close keep doing anyway, and choose it on purpose once — same time, same shape, deliberate. Say it belongs to both of you, and keep it even when it feels ordinary.
cells.core:
The pattern you carry is the one other people live inside — the way your people do things, the shape they keep. You've built plenty of it, and you describe it as simply how things are, found rather than made. Nobody around you has cause to say otherwise, so the credit keeps sitting with no one.

Go to the plainer thing underneath. This started as something you wanted to build with someone, before it hardened into how things are. Take one shared thing you already do and choose it on purpose — the same shape, decided this time. Say that it's yours together. What you made stays yours once you take it back from the background.
cells.sheetLine: The way your people do things is your doing, and you'd call it just how it is.
cells.verb: holding clear sight steady until what is true can be said well
cells.place: out past the literal, where only the shape of the thing remains

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the too-much person is building scaffolding others carry — the record says only calibrating with mature authority running ahead of timing; the reader could object that the pressure is internal, not something handed to others. The ask survives being wrong: whether or not others feel the weight, asking one person how it lands and taking down one piece is a real act either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is 'the structures are getting heavier than the walking' — it sounds good and says less than the plain thing.
